items.item: Each row shows the user's name and email, role, status in words (such as Active, Invited, Deactivated, Locked) and whether two-factor sign-in is enabled
items.evidence: rowHtml() renders name, mono email, role with dot(ROLE_DOT[u.role]), and status with dot(STATUS_DOT[u.status]) (e.g. 'Active'/'Invited'/'Suspended' as words) — but there is no 2FA column or indicator anywhere in rowHtml() or the users data model (mk() only stores name, email, role, status, lastSignIn).

items.item: Last sign-in uses one date-time format with the timezone stated, relative times also expose the exact time, and an account that has never signed in shows "Never" rather than a blank or a 1970 date
items.evidence: Last sign-in values are hardcoded relative strings mixing formats: '2 hours ago', 'Yesterday', 'Just now', '44 days ago' (mk() calls). The <td> just outputs u.lastSignIn with no title/tooltip attribute exposing an exact timestamp, and no timezone is stated anywhere. 'Never' is correctly shown for Elena Fischer/Benjamin Okafor/Yara Haddad, but the timezone/exact-time requirement is unmet.

items.item: Users can be found by searching name or email and filtered by role, status and inactivity (such as no sign-in for 90+ days), with the number of matching users shown
items.evidence: #searchInput filters by name/email and #roleFilter/#statusFilter filter by role and status (filteredUsers()), but there is no inactivity filter (e.g. 'no sign-in 90+ days') option anywhere. #accountSummary always renders the unfiltered total: 'users.length + ... accounts · ' + invitedCount + ' pending invites', never the filtered/match count.

items.item: The invite form requires an email and a role, labels both fields, and shows an inline error for a malformed address or one that already has an account
items.evidence: #inviteEmail has 'required' and type="email", and both fields have <label> elements, but the submit handler (inviteForm 'submit' listener) only reads the values and creates the user — there is no inline error element and no malformed/duplicate-email check anywhere in the script.

items.item: Deactivation asks for confirmation that names the user and states the effect (active sessions ended, sign-in blocked, data kept), and a deactivated user is offered Reactivate instead
items.evidence: openConfirm('deactivate') names the user in the title ('Deactivate ' + who + '?') but confirmBody only says 'They will immediately lose access to Fathom. You can reactivate the account at any time.' — it never explicitly states active sessions are ended or that data is kept. Reactivate is offered for Suspended users via menuItem('Reactivate account', 'reactivate', id).

items.item: The signed-in administrator's own row is marked (such as "You") and cannot be deactivated or lose the admin role, and the last remaining administrator cannot be deactivated, with the disabled action explaining why
items.evidence: The header shows the signed-in admin 'Priya Natarajan' (Owner), but rowHtml() never marks her row with 'You' or similar. openActionMenu() only special-cases role==='Owner' (hides Change role/Deactivate for the single Owner); every Admin (Marcus Webb, Sofia Marchetti, Hana Kobayashi, Oscar Lindgren) still gets a 'Deactivate account' item with no last-remaining-admin check or disabled/explained state.

items.item: Password reset sends a reset link to the user's email address, which the confirmation names, and the administrator never sees, sets or types the new password
items.evidence: doResetPassword() shows toast('Password reset email sent to ' + names[0] + '.') where names[0] is byId(id).name — the confirmation names the person, not the email address it was sent to. No password field is ever shown to the admin (pass criterion met for that part only).

items.item: Row actions are buttons or a keyboard-operable menu whose accessible names include the user (such as "Actions for Mai Nguyen"), and the outcome of an action is announced in an aria-live or role="status" region
items.evidence: The toggle button has aria-label='Actions for '+escapeHtml(u.name) (e.g. "Actions for Mai Nguyen"), satisfying the naming half. But outcomes are shown via toast(): '<div id="toastContainer" class="fixed bottom-4 right-4 z-[60] flex flex-col gap-2 items-end">' and the generated toast <div> — neither has aria-live or role="status", so action outcomes are not announced to assistive tech.

items.item: A search with no matching users shows a message with a way to clear it, and loading and failed-load states with a retry exist
items.evidence: render() shows 'No one matches your search. Try a different name, email, or filter.' when filteredUsers() is empty, but no clear/reset control is offered alongside it. There is no loading state and no failed-load/retry state anywhere in the script — users is a static in-memory array with no fetch logic at all.

notes: Data is a static in-memory array (no fetch/loading/error states by construction). Status model only has Active/Invited/Suspended — no 'Deactivated' or 'Locked' labels, and 'Suspended' is used as the deactivated state. Audit flagged 3 text-contrast failures on Last sign-in cells (3.22:1 vs 4.5:1 required) and that emails aren't mailto: links; no gradient/glass/emoji/uppercase-label template tells were detected and none were found on manual inspection — the page reads as a fairly bespoke, restrained admin UI rather than a templated dashboard.
